newsitem.title: USA: Soros says market reacts properly to WMX.
newsitem.headline: Soros says market reacts properly to WMX.

text.p: Soros Fund Management issued a statement late Tuesday saying market reaction to a restructuring proposal by WMX Technologies Inc was appropriate.
"Soros Fund Management believes that today's market reaction to the current management restructuring plan for WMX is appropriate," said Shawn Pattison, spokesman for Soros, a major WMX shareholder.
Shares in WMX closed off 3-1/8 to 33 on the New York Stock Exchange after it unveiled a sweeping restructuring plan.
"However, we strongly believe that the company has great assets and is substantially undervalued," Pattison said.
Pattison added, "If properly managed, the company has great potential."
George Soros' hedge-fund group owns about 5.2 percent of the outstanding shares of the Oak Brook, Ill.-based company, the largest U.S. garbage hauler and handler.
Soros and other major stockholders have been pressing WMX for months for improve its performance.

The company's restructuring plan includes selling off $1.5 billion in assets over the next two years, cutting 3,000 jobs, changing its name back to Waste Management Inc, reorganizing top management, buying back 50 million shares over two years, and cutting its capital budget.
